title: Too much blank space wasted at the top of each page -- allow `st.set_page_config( margin_top = 20 )`
body: I have a lot of data to present to the user. It doesn't fit vertically on the screen. It is frustrating to me that every single Streamlit page pushes my content down by 120pixels of blank space: Please allow something like: ```python st.set_page_config( initial_sidebar_state="expanded", margin_top = 20 ) ``` And while we are at it, some nice to haves: ```python st.set_page_config( initial_sidebar_state="expanded", margin_top = 20, margin_left = 20, margin_right = 10, margin_bottom=50, footer_text = "Creative Commons ... " ) ``` --- Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users. **If you'd like the Streamlit team to prioritize this feature request, please use the 👍 (thumbs up emoji) reaction in response to the initial post.** ![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-6336)

comments.body:
> I have a lot of data to present to the user. It doesn't fit vertically on the screen.

[USER] any chance you can share some screenshots or mocks of how your app looks like? That would help us figure out a good solution and prioritize this request. We currently don't have any plans to allow this level of customization. But we heard multiple requests for a "tight" layout mode in the past, so happy to think it through if it makes sense!

[USER] Right now I have private data that I cannot share but suffice it to say that I have a "drill down" cascade of related tables and graphs that take more vertical space than the screen allows and that require to scroll down (and I'd like to show more before requiring to scroll). The lower elements depend on selections in the upper elements (selections done with streamlit-aggrid so far). Making the tables smaller makes it too hard to find data. Splitting on multiple screens is too difficult (especially with url param bugs which I detailed in another issue).

However, what I wrote above was just a suggestion. If you make a "tight" layout with all "aesthetic margins" reduced to something like 10 or 20 pixels, I'll be happy with it :)

Thank you.

This is coming in Streamlit **1.66+** via theme variables, as implemented in #17350.

You can set the gap between the header and page content in `.streamlit/config.toml`:

```toml
[theme]
paddingTop = "1rem"
paddingBottom = "1rem"

# Optional — omit to inherit the [theme] values above
[theme.sidebar]
paddingTop = "1rem"
paddingBottom = "1rem"
```

Values are quoted `rem`, `px`, or a unitless number (`"0"` for zero padding).
